loc: For a site $\mathcal{C}$ and $U\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{C})$, let $\mathcal{C}/U$ be the slice site with coverings inherited from $\mathcal{C}$. The forgetful $j_U:\mathcal{C}/U\to\mathcal{C}$ induces a morphism of topoi with adjoints $j_{U!}\dashv j_U^{-1}\dashv j_{U*}$, and $j_U^{-1}$ is restriction.
hom: For sheaves $\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G}$ on a site $\mathcal{C}$, let $\SheafHom(\mathcal{F},\mathcal{G})$ be the sheaf with sections over $U$ equal to morphisms $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C}/U)(\mathcal{F}|_{\mathcal{C}/U},\mathcal{G}|_{\mathcal{C}/U})$.
glue: For a covering $\{U_i\to U\}$ in a site $\mathcal{C}$, gluing data consists of sheaves $\mathcal{F}_i$ on $\mathcal{C}/U_i$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_{ij}$ between their restrictions to $\mathcal{C}/(U_i\times_U U_j)$ satisfying $\varphi_{jk}\circ\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ on triple overlaps. Absolute gluing data on $\mathcal{C}$ means sheaves $\mathcal{F}_U$ on every slice $\mathcal{C}/U$ with compatible isomorphisms $j_f^{-1}\mathcal{F}_U\to\mathcal{F}_V$ for every arrow $f:V\to U$, satisfying the composition cocycle.
reloc: For a site $\mathcal{C}$ and arrow $f:U\to V$, the induced functor $j_{U/V}:\mathcal{C}/U\to\mathcal{C}/V$ sends $(X\to U)$ to $(X\to U\to V)$. It is a continuous and cocontinuous morphism of sites and induces the corresponding morphism of topoi, with $j_U=j_V\circ j_{U/V}$ on sites and topoi.
site_morphism: A morphism of sites $f:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ is given by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal{D}\to\mathcal{C}$ with exact sheaf-valued left adjoint $u_s=f^{-1}$; the pushforward is $f_*=u^s$. For a site $\mathcal{E}$ and $W\in\mathcal{E}$, write $j_W$ for localization to $\mathcal{E}/W$. The standard equivalence $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{E}/W)\simeq\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{E})/h_W^\#$ identifies slice-site sheaves with sheaves over the associated representable.
pu: For a functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ and $V\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal{D})$, the category $({}_V^u\mathcal{I})$ has objects $(U,\psi:u(U)\to V)$ and arrows $\alpha:U\to U'$ with $\psi=\psi'\circ u(\alpha)$. This is the right-indexing category for the right Kan extension $({}_pu)$. For cocontinuous $u$ the associated morphism of topoi has $f_*=({}_su)$ and $f^{-1}=(u^p-)^\#$.
coc: A cocontinuous functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ induces a morphism of topoi $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{D})$, with $f_*=({}_su)$ and $f^{-1}\mathcal{G}=(u^p\mathcal{G})^\#$. If $u$ is also continuous the inverse image is exact and has left adjoint $f_!$.
special: A special cocontinuous functor $u:\mathcal{C}\to\mathcal{D}$ is a functor which is cocontinuous and continuous and satisfies: (3) arrows in $\mathcal{C}$ identified by $u$ are made equal after some covering of their common source; (4) each arrow $u(U')\to u(U)$ lifts locally along a covering of $U'$; (5) every object of $\mathcal{D}$ has a covering by objects of the form $u(U_i)$. These conditions guarantee that its associated morphism of topoi is an equivalence.
toposloc: For a sheaf $\mathcal{F}$ on a site $\mathcal{C}$, the slice category $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})/\mathcal{F}$ is a topos with canonical localization morphism $j_{\mathcal{F}}$ to $\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal{C})$. Its inverse image sends $\mathcal{H}$ to $(\mathcal{H}\times\mathcal{F}\to\mathcal{F})$, its left adjoint sends $(\mathcal{G}\to\mathcal{F})$ to $\mathcal{G}$, and it has right adjoint $j_{\mathcal{F}*}$. If $\mathcal{F}=h_U^\#$, then this slice localization identifies with the site localization $\mathcal{C}/U$.
